name: Marrakech
label: Imperial Capital
shortDesc: The bustling Red City where centuries of history meet vibrant souks, tranquil riads, and Jemaa el-Fna.
overview: Marrakech is a feast for all senses. Founded in 1062 by the Almoravids, its red clay ramparts shelter lush hidden courtyards, aromatic spice markets, and grand Islamic architecture. As the sun sets, the legendary Jemaa el-Fna square comes alive with storytellers, musicians, and sizzling food stalls.

Vibrant Spice Souks of the Old Medina
Bahia Palace Moorish Archways
Tranquil Riad Courtyard with Zellige Fountain
Ancient Clay Ramparts at Sunset
Intricate Moroccan Zellige Ceramic Tiles

landmarks.name: Jemaa el-Fna Square
landmarks.desc: UNESCO Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage

landmarks.name: Bahia Palace
landmarks.desc: 19th-century masterpiece of Islamic and Moroccan decorative arts

landmarks.name: Koutoubia Mosque
landmarks.desc: The 77-meter iconic minaret dominating the city skyline

landmarks.name: Majorelle Garden
landmarks.desc: Cobalt blue botanical sanctuary created by Jacques Majorelle

food.name: Tanjia Marrakchia
food.desc: Slow-cooked spiced beef or lamb in a clay urn beneath the hammam ashes.

food.name: Pastilla
food.desc: Delicate crispy filo pastry layered with spiced meat, cinnamon, and toasted almonds.

food.name: Mint Tea with Sheeba
food.desc: Traditional gunpowder green tea steeped with fresh spearmint and wormwood.

culture: Marrakech celebrates artisanal craftsmanship with over 40 distinct artisan guilds in the souks, from leather tanners to copper beaters and cedarwood carvers.
tips: Bargain with a friendly smile in the souks — counter-offer roughly half and negotiate warmly.
Stay inside a traditional riad in the Medina for an authentic and peaceful oasis experience.
Visit popular sites like Bahia Palace and Majorelle early morning to avoid peak crowds.

name: Chefchaouen
label: The Blue Pearl
shortDesc: Nestled between the peaks of the Rif Mountains, famous worldwide for its serene blue-washed alleyways.
overview: Founded in 1471 as a fortress against Portuguese invasions, Chefchaouen is legendary for its tranquil blue-painted alleyways and mountain backdrop. Jewish refugees and Andalusian Muslims shaped its distinctive architecture, tinting walls in shades of sky blue to symbolize peace and spirituality.

gallery.caption: Famous Blue-Washed Medina Alleyways
Blue Steps Decorated with Clay Flowerpots
Charming Indigo Passageways in the Old Town
Handcrafted Blue Wooden Doors
Rif Mountain Peaks Framing the Valley
View from the Spanish Mosque at Golden Hour

landmarks.name: Plaza Uta el-Hammam
landmarks.desc: The atmospheric main square lined with cafes and red-stone kasbah

landmarks.name: The Spanish Mosque
landmarks.desc: Hilltop lookout offering breathtaking sunset views over the blue medina

landmarks.name: Ras El Maa Waterfall
landmarks.desc: Fresh mountain springs where locals gather and wash rugs

landmarks.name: Kasbah Museum
landmarks.desc: Restored 15th-century fortress featuring Andalusian gardens and ethnography

food.name: Jben (Fresh Goat Cheese)
food.desc: Tangy local mountain goat cheese served with fresh olive oil and herbs.

food.name: Bissara Soup
food.desc: Hearty fava bean soup laced with cumin, garlic, and fresh extra virgin olive oil.

food.name: Mountain Honey & Figs
food.desc: Wild thyme honey gathered from the surrounding Rif valleys.

culture: Renowned for handwoven Berber wool blankets (mendil) with distinctive red, white, and blue stripes, and delicate cedarwood pottery.
tips: Wear comfortable walking shoes with grip; the cobbled alleys can be steep and slick.
Hike up to the Spanish Mosque 45 minutes before sunset for the most photogenic panorama.
Respect residents by asking permission before photographing people or private doorways.

name: Fès
label: Spiritual Capital
shortDesc: The spiritual and intellectual heart of Morocco, home to the worlds oldest university and medieval medina.
overview: Founded in the 8th century, Fès el-Bali is the worlds largest car-free urban area and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Stepping through the blue tile gates of Bab Bou Jeloud transports you into a living medieval civilization of over 9,000 labyrinthine alleyways, sacred mosques, and aromatic spice souks.

gallery.caption: Bab Bou Jeloud (The Famous Blue Gate)
Chouara Leather Tanneries from the Terraces
Labyrinth of Fès el-Bali Medieval Medina
Bou Inania Medersa Carved Stucco and Zellige
Al Quaraouiyine University Marble Court
Fassi Cobalt Blue Ceramic Pottery

landmarks.name: Chouara Tannery
landmarks.desc: 11th-century open-air stone dyeing pits producing world-renowned Moroccan leather

landmarks.name: Al Quaraouiyine University
landmarks.desc: Founded in 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri, the oldest continually operating university in the world

landmarks.name: Bou Inania Medersa
landmarks.desc: Exquisite 14th-century Marinid theological college with intact clock tower

landmarks.name: Bab Bou Jeloud Gate
landmarks.desc: Grand Moorish entrance tiled in blue on the outside and green inside

food.name: Pastilla Fassi
food.desc: The definitive Fassi luxury dish: shredded pigeon or chicken layered with spiced almonds and orange blossom water.

food.name: Lamb Tagine with Prunes
food.desc: Tender braised lamb slow-cooked with caramelized prunes, toasted almonds, and sesame.

food.name: Khlea
food.desc: Cured spiced beef dried in the sun and preserved in olive oil, traditionally eaten with eggs.

culture: Fes is the artisan capital of Moroccan ceramics, famous worldwide for Fassi cobalt blue pottery, intricate zellige mosaics, and hammered brass lanterns.
tips: Hire an official licensed guide for your first morning to master the Medinas 9,000 alleys without getting lost.
Accept the mint sprig offered by tannery shopkeepers — holding it to your nose counters the strong leather curing scents.
Visit the Pottery Cooperative of Ain Nokbi just outside the medina to watch master artisans at work.

name: Tangier
label: Gateway of Africa
shortDesc: Where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, steeped in cosmopolitan romance, coastal views, and legendary literary history.
overview: Perched on the Strait of Gibraltar just 14 kilometers from Spain, Tangier has captivated artists, writers, and travelers for decades. Once a legendary international zone, the modern city blends bohemian cafes, whitewashed kasbah battlements, and the meeting point of two seas.

gallery.caption: Cap Spartel Lighthouse Where Atlantic Meets Mediterranean
Tangier Coastal Bay & Corniche at Dusk
Whitewashed Alleys in the Historic Kasbah
Waves Crashing against the Straits of Gibraltar
Grand Socco & Cinema Rif Moorish Architecture
Sandy Coastline of Achakar Beach

landmarks.name: Cap Spartel & Lighthouse
landmarks.desc: The northwestern tip of Africa where the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea merge

landmarks.name: Caves of Hercules
landmarks.desc: Mythological sea-cavern whose opening to the ocean mirrors the outline of Africa

landmarks.name: The Kasbah & Museum
landmarks.desc: Former sultans palace with panoramic views across the Strait to Spain

landmarks.name: Café Hafa
landmarks.desc: Historic cliffside open-air cafe frequented by Paul Bowles and The Rolling Stones

food.name: Fresh Mediterranean Fish Tagine
food.desc: Catch of the day with chermoula marinade, bell peppers, tomatoes, and preserved lemon.

food.name: Bocadillo Tanjawi
food.desc: Famous Tangier street sandwich stuffed with tuna, boiled egg, fries, olives, and harissa.

food.name: Mint Tea with Pine Nuts
food.desc: Northern Moroccan specialty tea served in the cliffside cafes of Cap Spartel.

culture: A unique cultural crossroads connecting Andalusian music, international diplomacy, Mediterranean seafood traditions, and contemporary art.
tips: Take the Al Boraq high-speed train for a fast, scenic 2-hour trip connecting Tangier to Casablanca or Rabat.
Spend late afternoon at Café Hafa sipping mint tea while watching ferry boats cross to Spain.
Stroll through the Petit Socco to enjoy authentic vintage coffee shops and lively conversation.

name: Essaouira
label: Atlantic Fort & Port
shortDesc: A relaxed Atlantic coastal haven celebrated for 18th-century sea ramparts, fresh seafood, and soulful Gnaoua music.
overview: Formerly known as Mogador, Essaouira is an Atlantic seaside fortress designed in 1760 by a French military architect for Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah. Known for its steady trade winds, squawking gulls, vibrant blue fishing skiffs, and relaxed artistic tempo, it offers an idyllic coastal escape.

gallery.caption: Skala de la Kasbah Ramparts with Bronze Cannons

Wide Golden Sand Beach and Camel Rides

Thuya Wood Carving Workshops and Souks

landmarks.name: Skala du Port & Ramparts
landmarks.desc: Historic stone ramparts with ocean views across the Atlantic bastions

landmarks.name: The Fishing Port
landmarks.desc: Bustling harbor where fishermen haul blue wooden boats and grill fresh sardines

landmarks.name: Mogador Island
landmarks.desc: Protected nature reserve and sanctuary for rare Eleonoras falcons

landmarks.name: Thuya Wood Crafts Guild
landmarks.desc: Famous artisan workshops carving aromatic burl thuya root wood

food.name: Fresh Grilled Sardines
food.desc: Caught morning of, tossed on open coals with lemon juice and cumin salt.

food.name: Fish Tagine with Argan Oil
food.desc: Atlantic sea bass or monkfish cooked in clay tagine drizzled with culinary argan oil.

food.name: Argan Oil & Amlou
food.desc: Creamy Moroccan spread made from roasted almonds, pure argan oil, and wild honey.

culture: The spiritual birthplace of Gnaoua music — a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage blending sub-Saharan spiritual rhythms and Berber poetry.
tips: Bring a light windbreaker or sweater even in mid-summer; the Atlantic trade wind (Alizee) keeps it breezy.
Select your fresh seafood directly at the port stalls to have it cooked on the spot for lunch.
Take a beginner kitesurfing or horse-riding lesson along the wide sandy beach.

name: Merzouga
label: Jewel of the Sahara
shortDesc: Awe-inspiring Sahara Desert dunes reaching up to 150 meters high, camel caravans, and starlit Berber camps.
overview: Merzouga is the gateway to Erg Chebbi, Moroccos most majestic dune sea. Watching the apricot-gold sands shift into deep violet as the Saharan sun dips below the horizon, followed by a sky glittering with millions of stars around a desert campfire, is an unforgettable experience.
weather: Sunny Warm Days, Crisp Starry Nights

gallery.caption: Erg Chebbi Majestic Sand Dunes at Sunset
Camel Caravan Trekking across Golden Ridges

Milky Way and Crystal Clear Stargazing Skies
Gateway to the Great Dunes of Tafilalet
Traditional Saharan Mint Tea & Desert Spices

landmarks.name: Erg Chebbi Dunes
landmarks.desc: Moroccos tallest golden dunes shifting colors continuously with the sun

landmarks.name: Khamlia Gnawa Village
landmarks.desc: Desert community famous for soulful live Gnawa music and hospitality

landmarks.name: Dayet Srji Flamingo Lake
landmarks.desc: Seasonal desert lake attracting flocks of pink flamingos in winter and spring

landmarks.name: Rissani Mausoleum & Date Souk
landmarks.desc: Ancient trading post on the trans-Saharan caravan route

food.name: Medfouna (Berber Pizza)
food.desc: Stuffed desert bread baked in sand ovens with spiced minced beef, almonds, and herbs.

food.name: Desert Camp Tagine
food.desc: Clay pot cooked over glowing charcoal in the sand, scented with cumin, ginger, and saffron.

food.name: Dates of Tafilalet
food.desc: Sweet, rich Medjool dates harvested from the surrounding desert palmeries.

culture: Deeply rooted in nomadic Berber traditions, camel husbandry, celestial navigation, and warm hospitality around the evening fire.
tips: Pack warm layers — desert nights can drop below 10°C even after sunny 25°C days.
Opt for a desert camp with private en-suite tents and solar power for maximum comfort.
Wake up before dawn for a sunrise trek up the high ridge — the colors are unforgettable.

name: Agadir & Taghazout
label: Sun & Atlantic Surf
shortDesc: Moroccos premier coastal resort with 300 days of sunshine, world-class surf breaks, and sandy crescent bays.
overview: Blessed with 300 days of annual sunshine and a wide 10-kilometer golden beach, Agadir is Moroccos modern seaside capital. Just 20 minutes north lies the world-famous surf village of Taghazout, where surfers from around the globe ride legendary point breaks.

gallery.caption: Agadir 10-Kilometer Golden Beach Crescent

Paradise Valley Natural Rock Pools & Palms

landmarks.name: Agadir Oufella Kasbah
landmarks.desc: 16th-century hilltop citadel featuring panoramic views across the bay

landmarks.name: Taghazout Bay & Anchor Point
landmarks.desc: Legendary surf mecca with right-hand point breaks and chill bohemian cafes

landmarks.name: Souk El Had
landmarks.desc: One of the largest markets in Africa with over 6,000 stalls of spices and crafts

landmarks.name: Paradise Valley
landmarks.desc: Mountain oasis 45 minutes inland with emerald rock pools and palm groves

food.name: Argan Tagine of the Souss
food.desc: Slow-cooked local chicken with preserved lemons and organic Souss argan oil.

food.name: Grilled Sea Bream & Calamari
food.desc: Fresh seafood prepared on the beachfront boardwalk with homemade harissa.

food.name: Amlou on Warm Msemmen
food.desc: Rich dip of roasted almonds, pure argan oil, and blossom honey served on flaky flatbread.

culture: Center of Amazigh (Berber) culture in the fertile Souss Valley, celebrated for silver jewelry and argan cooperatives.
tips: Take the modern cable car up to the restored Agadir Oufella Kasbah at sunset.
Visit an authentic women-led argan oil cooperative on the road to Taghazout.
Rent a surfboard or book a surf coaching lesson in Taghazout.

name: Rabat
label: Modern Capital & UNESCO Heritage
shortDesc: Moroccos elegant capital combining tree-lined boulevards, coastal ocean fortress, and UNESCO-listed monuments.
overview: Named a UNESCO World Heritage site, Rabat is one of Moroccos four Imperial Cities. It offers a sophisticated atmosphere with clean coastal air, the dramatic 12th-century Hassan Tower, and the cliffside Kasbah of the Udayas.

gallery.caption: Hassan Tower Red Sandstone Columns & Minaret
Andalusian Gardens of the Kasbah of the Udayas
Blue and White Alleys of the Kasbah of the Udayas
Royal Palace Monumental Archway
Bouregreg Marina & Mohammed VI Tower
Mausoleum of Mohammed V Royal Craftsmanship

landmarks.name: Hassan Tower & Mausoleum
landmarks.desc: 12th-century minaret and tomb of the royal kings guarded by royal horsemen

landmarks.name: Kasbah of the Udayas
landmarks.desc: 12th-century cliffside fortress with blue-and-white houses and ocean vistas

landmarks.name: Chellah Necropolis
landmarks.desc: Ancient Roman ruins of Sala Colonia intertwined with medieval Marinid royal tombs

landmarks.name: Grand Theatre of Rabat
landmarks.desc: Futuristic architectural masterpiece designed by Zaha Hadid

food.name: Couscous Bidawi with Seven Vegetables
food.desc: Fluffy steamed semolina topped with pumpkin, turnips, carrots, and chickpeas.

food.name: Kaab el Ghazal (Gazelle Horns)
food.desc: Delicate crescent pastries filled with almond paste scented with orange blossom.

food.name: Harira Soup with Dates
food.desc: Rich tomato, lentil, and chickpea broth traditionally served with honeyed chebakia.

culture: A calm, prestigious cultural center hosting the National Museum of Modern Art and pristine embassies.
tips: Rabat is very walkable and has modern trams connecting the capital across the river to Salé.
Visit the Café Maure in the Kasbah of the Udayas for mint tea with a panoramic view of the river mouth.
Dress respectfully when visiting the Mausoleum of Mohammed V.

name: Ifrane
label: Little Switzerland of Morocco
shortDesc: A picturesque alpine resort in the Middle Atlas featuring cedar forests, Swiss-style chalets, and winter snow.
overview: Located at 1,665 meters altitude in the Middle Atlas, Ifrane was built in the 1930s. Often called the Switzerland of Morocco, it boasts red-roofed alpine chalets, pristine flower-lined parks, Europe-like cleanliness, and nearby ski slopes at Michlifen.
season: Year-round (Autumn & Winter for snow; Spring for greenery)
weather: Crisp Alpine Air (0°C in Winter, 22°C in Summer)

gallery.caption: Pristine Cedar and Pine Mountains of the Middle Atlas
Cèdre Gouraud Ancient Forest Near Azrou
Alpine Snow Chalets and Ski Resort of Michlifen
Snow-Dusted Middle Atlas Mountain Horizon
Green Valleys and Springs around Ifrane National Park
Tranquil Lakeside Gardens of Al Akhawayn University

landmarks.name: The Stone Lion of Ifrane
landmarks.desc: Famous sculpture carved into living boulder commemorating the extinct Atlas Lion

landmarks.name: Cèdre Gouraud Forest (Azrou)
landmarks.desc: Century-old cedar forest home to wild Barbary macaque monkeys

landmarks.name: Michlifen Ski Station
landmarks.desc: Volcanic crater ski resort situated at 2,000 meters altitude

landmarks.name: Vittel Spring & Waterfalls
landmarks.desc: Peaceful forested pathway leading to freshwater mountain springs

food.name: Atlas Mountain Trout
food.desc: Fresh trout caught in cold mountain streams and grilled with fresh herbs.

food.name: Middle Atlas Wild Mushroom Tagine
food.desc: Seasonal morel and boletus mushrooms braised with tender beef.

food.name: Hot Spiced Mint Tea with Mountain Thyme
food.desc: Warming herbal tea infused with wild thyme and pennyroyal.

culture: A unique blend of clean alpine university town culture and traditional Berber pastoral life from nearby Azrou.
tips: Visit the nearby Azrou cedar forest to see friendly Barbary macaques in their natural habitat.
Great stopover destination when traveling between Fes and the Sahara Desert.
In winter (Dec-Feb), pack warm winter coats, gloves, and boots.

name: Al Hoceima
label: Mediterranean Turquoise Jewel
shortDesc: Crystal-clear turquoise Mediterranean waters framed by the dramatic red cliffs of the Rif Mountains.
overview: Overlooking one of the most stunning Mediterranean bays in North Africa, Al Hoceima combines turquoise waters, hidden coves, and pristine national parks. Its Spanish-influenced plazas and fresh grilled seafood make it a sublime coastal paradise.

gallery.caption: Plage Quemado Turquoise Water and Cliffs

Cala Bonita Cove with Crystal Calm Seas
Mediterranean Clear Blue Waters
Scenic Clifftop Promenades and Sunset Views
Al Hoceima Harbor and Fishing Skiffs

landmarks.name: Plage Quemado
landmarks.desc: The iconic golden sand cove situated right at the foot of dramatic cliff walls

landmarks.name: Al Hoceima National Park
landmarks.desc: Coastal park sanctuary for rare osprey birds, dolphins, and unspoiled coves

landmarks.name: Plage Asfiha & Spanish Rock
landmarks.desc: Panoramic beach looking directly across at Peñón de Alhucemas

landmarks.name: Cala Bonita
landmarks.desc: Peaceful turquoise cove ideal for family swimming and snorkeling

food.name: Mediterranean Espeto de Sardinas
food.desc: Fresh sardines skewered on canes and barbecued over open beach fires.

food.name: Rifian Paella & Seafood Platter
food.desc: Seafood rice dish bursting with local shrimp, squid, and clams.

food.name: Fresh Fig & Cactus Fruit
food.desc: Sweet prickly pears harvested fresh from coastal Rif slopes.

culture: Proud Amazigh Rifian maritime culture, where Berber traditions merge with Mediterranean lifestyle.
tips: Rent a kayak or take a boat tour to explore secret sea caves in Al Hoceima National Park.
Visit in June or September for tranquil beaches without midsummer holiday crowds.
Try snorkeling at Cala Bonita where waters are calm and transparent.

name: Ouarzazate & Aït Benhaddou
label: Door of the Desert & UNESCO Ksar
shortDesc: Legendary clay kasbahs, cinema studios, and the iconic UNESCO World Heritage fortress of Aït Benhaddou.
overview: Known as the Door of the Desert, Ouarzazate is famed for its monumental earthen architecture and global film studios. Nearby stands the majestic Ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site and backdrop for Gladiator and Lawrence of Arabia.

landmarks.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou
landmarks.desc: 11th-century UNESCO fortified clay village on the trans-Saharan caravan route

landmarks.name: Atlas Film Studios
landmarks.desc: One of the worlds largest movie production lots with Egyptian and Roman sets

landmarks.name: Kasbah Taourirt
landmarks.desc: Historic residence of the Glaoui pasha featuring ornate clay rooms

landmarks.name: Ounila Valley
landmarks.desc: Spectacular canyon road linking Aït Benhaddou to the High Atlas

food.name: Tagine of Camel Meat & Figs
food.desc: Slow-braised camel meat with desert figs, wild cumin, and sweet onions.

food.name: Ouarzazate Saffron Couscous
food.desc: Golden semolina scented with pure Taliouine saffron and organic vegetables.

food.name: Berber Bread with Olive Oil
food.desc: Fresh baked clay-oven flatbread dipped in local Draa olive oil.

culture: Centuries of southern Moroccan Glaoua history, caravan trade lore, and traditional mud-brick earthen architecture.
tips: Cross the river stones early in the morning to explore Aït Benhaddou before tour buses arrive.
Climb to the ruined granary at the summit of Aït Benhaddou for an extraordinary 360° valley view.
Tour Atlas Film Studios for behind-the-scenes movie sets.

name: High Atlas & Imlil (Toubkal)
label: Roof of North Africa
shortDesc: Gateway to Mount Toubkal (4,167m), terraced Berber villages, rushing mountain rivers, and alpine hiking.
overview: Rising just 90 minutes south of Marrakech, the High Atlas Mountains form the dramatic spine of Morocco. The village of Imlil serves as the premier mountain trekking base, where terraced apple orchards, stone Berber houses, and mule tracks lead toward Mount Toubkal.

Berber Hospitality with Freshly Steeped Mint Tea

landmarks.name: Mount Toubkal Peak (4,167m)
landmarks.desc: Highest mountain peak in North Africa and the Arab world

landmarks.name: Aroumd Village
landmarks.desc: Traditional village built on a spur of rock with views across the Mizane Valley

landmarks.name: Tizi n’Tichka Pass
landmarks.desc: Breathtaking 2,260-meter mountain pass connecting Marrakech to the south

landmarks.name: Ourika Valley Waterfalls
landmarks.desc: Lush green valley with natural cascades and riverside cafes

food.name: Berber Tagine on Open Fire
food.desc: Conical earthenware tagine packed with mountain vegetables, wild herbs, and goat meat.

food.name: Fresh Walnuts & Mountain Honey
food.desc: Locally harvested Atlas walnuts served with warm bread and wild thyme honey.

food.name: High Atlas Herb Tea
food.desc: Infused with mountain sage, pennyroyal, and spearmint.

culture: Authentic Berber highland culture emphasizing community solidarity, terraced agriculture, and mountain hospitality.
tips: Hiring an official registered mountain guide is mandatory for the Mount Toubkal summit trek.
Pack sturdy hiking boots, sun protection, and a warm fleece for cool mountain evenings.
Stop for lunch at a riverside Berber cafe in the Ourika Valley.
